To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a high erythrocyte n-6 FA content is associated with a decreased risk of HCC, while a high n-3 FA content is associated neither with an increased nor with a decreased risk.
the fatty acid composition of the membrane of erythrocytes, a surrogate of the fatty acid composition in the liver, was associated with risk of HCC in cirrhotics.

1) the erythrocytes are an excellent source of information on the FA composition of the body; 2) the erythrocellular membrane FA composition reflects the dietary FA composition; 3) in cirrhosis the erythrocellar membrane FA composition reflects both the dietary FA composition and the FA composition of hepatic lipids; 4) the erythro cell membrane FA composition is related to HCC risk in cirrhotics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Fatty Acid Synthase (FAS) in cancer.
the role of the membrane fatty acid composition of red blood cells (RBCs) as a marker of the fatty acid composition of the cell membrane in the development of HCC in cirrhotics.
the study of the role of Fatty acids (FA) in hepatocellular carcinoma development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the association of FA with HCC is complex and that the role of individual FA in the development of HCC is still unclear.
there is a lack of evidence that FA composition of the erythocyte membrane is associated with HCC risk in cirrhosis.
the association of FAs with HCC is still inconclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a significant correlation between the erythrocytes membrane FA composition and HCC risk.
the erythrocytes of patients with HCC had a higher proportion of polyunsaturated FAs and a lower proportion of saturated FAs than those of cirrhotic controls.
the fatty acid composition in the erythrocytes membrane of patients with cirrhosis and HCC is different from those of patients with cirrhotic without HCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the erythrocytes are an accessible source of biomarkers for FA composition and that this is an important source of information for cancer prevention and treatment.
the erythrocytes are an accessible and stable source for the determination of the fatty acid composition of the cell membrane.
the FA composition of erythrocyte membranes is a promising tool for identifying individuals at risk of HCC.
